body_markdown:
TL;DR


Hitting $100k in roofing sales comes down to three things: knowing what you're selling, mastering a repeatable sales process, and building a follow-up system that actually works.


Wanna know how to sell roofs like the pros do? The process isn't magic — it's structured, repeatable, and learnable. Most roofers who hit $100k follow five core steps, but the one that separates them from the rest is follow-up. Eighty percent of roofing sales don't happen on the first contact. They happen on the fifth contact or later. That's not random — that's a system.


## Know what you're selling


Before learning how to sell roofs, you need to understand what you're selling and why it matters to the customer.


Roofing's all about solving problems. That mindset shift makes a big difference in closing deals.


### Common roofing materials:


- **Asphalt shingles** – Affordable, popular, and used all over North America. Great for homeowners on a budget. Low maintenance, but have a short lifespan.
- **Metal roofing** – Durable, weather-resistant, and fireproof. Growing in demand. Lightweight and easy to transport. Life expectancy of 40 to 70 years. Big margins here.
- **Clay tiles** – Great for hot, dry climates, since they don't expand and contract as temperatures change. Long lifespan, but heavier and pricier.
- **Slate** – Premium, with a great natural look. Weather-resistant. Doesn't need much maintenance, but can be expensive. Ideal for higher-end projects.


When you're talking to homeowners about roofing materials, don't focus on the technical specs. Talk about how the product solves a problem: This roof is more durable. Won't leak. Lasts a long time. Energy efficient. Has curb appeal.


## Qualifying as a roofing salesperson


*Technically* , all you need is a high school diploma to start working as a salesperson.


Buuuut… previous experience in construction or roofing is pretty important too. It helps you understand the market and compete properly. You need to be an expert on what you're selling, so if you haven't spent much time on a roof yet, do that first.


For most folks, the path into roofing sales starts with a roofing apprenticeship or by learning from someone who's done it.


## What is the five-step roofing sales process?


Hitting $100k starts with mastering the basics and refining them into a repeatable process.


### Step 1. Generate and qualify leads


Use digital ads, referrals, and[Google Business Profiles](https://roofr.com/blog/roofers-guide-google-business-profile) to fill your pipeline. Lead generation is the single most time-consuming activity for roofing businesses—and also the most challenging. So systems matter here.


### Step 2. Build trust before selling


Homeowners buy from[local folks they trust](https://roofr.com/blog/neighborhood-roofer-explained) . Your credibility is your currency. Show up professionally, listen more than you talk, and prove you know your stuff.


### Step 3. Present a professional proposal


Create[branded, professional Proposals](https://roofr.com/proposals) with visuals and pricing breakdowns. This isn't optional—your proposal is often the deciding factor.


### Step 4. Handle objections the right way


Take time to put homeowners at ease and[explain the costs line by line](https://roofr.com/blog/itemized-roofing-quotes) . Address their concerns head-on, don't gloss over them.


### Step 5. Follow up, again and again


This is where most roofers fail. Consistent follow-up separates the $100k earners from the rest.


## The follow-up cadence that actually works


Here's the truth: 80% of roofing sales don't happen on the first contact. They happen on the fifth contact—or later.


Most contractors lose deals because they stop reaching out too early. A structured follow-up system is the difference between winning and losing $10k-$50k+ in jobs.


### The 7-touch 30-day system


For leads who've received an estimate or proposal, use this proven cadence:


1. **Same-day recap** (within hours) – Send a text or email summarizing your conversation, the proposal link, and next steps.
2. **Next-day call** (24 hours) – A quick call to answer any questions and confirm they received the proposal.
3. **Day 3 value message** – Send a text with a case study, review, or photo of similar work you've done nearby.
4. **Day 7 decision call** – Call to ask if they have questions or need clarification. Don't be pushy; be helpful.
5. **Day 14 proof email** – Email with warranty info, material specs, or a customer testimonial addressing common objections.
6. **Day 21 timeline call** – Check in on their timeline. "When were you hoping to get started?"
7. **Day 30 close-the-loop email** – Final message. If they've gone silent, respect that and keep their info for future touchpoints.


**Key principle:** Every touch should add value or move the conversation forward. "Just checking in" doesn't count.


### Why automation matters


Manual follow-up is killing your close rates. Roofing companies using automated follow-up sequences see 2–3× higher lead-to-job conversion compared to those relying on manual outreach alone.


Why? Because when you're busy with other jobs, follow-ups slip. With automation, reminders never slip.


### What if they don't sign at the appointment?


Start the follow-up sequence immediately. Don't wait until tomorrow. The first 24 hours matter most.


And respect what they tell you. If they say "Call me in two weeks," don't call on day 3. If they choose another contractor, let them go. Use Roofr CRM to track their decision and update their status so your team knows not to spam them.


## Roofing sales tips for hitting six figures


Here are the best practices that separate top reps from the rest:


### How fast should you respond to roofing leads?


Homeowners who ask for an estimate aren't browsing for fun. They're ready to talk NOW.


[Response times under five minutes work best](https://www.vectorfirmacademy.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/Best-Practices-for-Lead-Response-Harvard-Business-Review.pdf) , though most companies still miss that window.


**How to make it work:**


- Use call routing, instant text replies, and automations.
- Keep calls short and effective by being direct, honest, and straight-to-the-point.
- If you miss the first window, don't give up. Keep following up over the next few days.


### Should you show three options or one proposal?


A single price forces a yes or no. Three choices invite a conversation.


*Good, better, best* packages nudge most buyers to the middle tier and often increase average job size. Multi-option proposals will earn you more work *and* raise your revenue.


**How to package it:**


- **Good.** Three-tab or entry architectural. Basic underlayment. Standard ventilation.
- **Better.** Arch shingles with enhanced wind rating. Ice and water at eaves and valleys. Better ventilation.
- **Best.** Class 3 or Class 4 impact-resistant shingles. Synthetic underlayment. Upgraded metal. Extended workmanship warranty.


### Should you send videos or PDFs to homeowners?


Most homeowners won't read a long PDF. A two-minute video that explains scope, warranty, and timeline works better.


In your video, walk the homeowner through the price breakdown line by line, use visuals like similar houses, and explain why ventilation and underlayment matter.


### How important are customer reviews in roofing sales?


People scan stars before they answer your call. Homeowners expect the same from you.


**Make reviews part of the roofing sales process:**


- Ask every customer within two weeks of completion.
- Use automated text and email templates.
- Reply publicly to every review, even if it's just a "thanks for your business!"


### How do you nail the in-home sales flow?


Little things move big numbers. Here's a tight script for reps learning how to sell roofs.


- Before the visit, confirm the appointment by text. Share a short bio and photo so they know who is coming.
- When you arrive, set expectations. "We still good for 25 minutes?"
- Listen to the homeowner's concerns. Then ask: "What would make this easy for you?"
- Present three options, starting with what you'd put on your own house. "Which option fits how long you plan to stay in the home?"
- Book a decision or a follow-up time on the spot.
- Send a same-day recap with your proposal link.


### When should you focus your sales efforts?


Whether you're sending emails or going door-to-door, be smart about where and when you focus your energy.


- Pay attention to wind and hail, then get to the hardest-hit spots immediately.
- Use local proof. "We just finished two roofs down the street. Check out these photos."
- Offer same-day measurements and multi-option estimates with no obligation.
- Keep circling back (without being too pushy). If someone says not right now, that means maybe in the future.
